findings.what: The round-3 non-vacuity claim is misreported for the one test that pins the round-2 blocking fix. The author's comment states 'All five failures behavioural ... no ImportError/AttributeError', but test_phase_major_document_status_is_demoted_by_the_sweep fails at dc0f13f with AttributeError: 'PageState' object has no attribute 'fabricated_image_refs' at its setup assert (test line 371), before _phase_assemble is ever called. I reproduced this exactly (see access_proof): 5 failed / 5 passed matches, but one failure is a symbol-absence error, not the quoted 'still finished SUCCESS'. This is the same trap the author caught in round 2 (its own round-2 comment describes fixing identical direct-attribute asserts with getattr) and has now reintroduced in the new test. The fix is one line: use getattr(state.pages[1], 'fabricated_image_refs', 0) in the setup assert and re-run the baseline so the ordering proof is behavioural as claimed. Note: the code change itself is NOT in doubt — the test at head drives the real _phase_assemble and genuinely pins the ordering (a sweep running after pages_ok would leave status SUCCESS and fail it), and the author separately reproduced the behavioural failure against the previous head 7696719. What is void is the baseline proof as stated against dc0f13f.
findings.why: The board's evidence rule is that a non-vacuity proof must fail on behaviour, not on a symbol the PR itself adds; this PR has been caught by that trap twice tonight and the round-3 comment asserts, falsely, that it did not happen again.
